question.text: The speed of sound in oxygen $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$ at a certain temperature is $460 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. The speed of sound in helium (He) at the same temperature will be (assumed both gases to be ideal)

solution.text:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& v=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}} \\
& \frac{V_1}{V_2}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma_1 M_2}{\gamma_2 M_1}}=\sqrt{\frac{\frac{7}{5} \times 4}{\frac{5}{3} \times 32}} \\
& \frac{460}{V_2}=\sqrt{\frac{21}{25 \times 8}} \Rightarrow \quad v_2=\frac{460 \times 5 \times 2 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{21}}=1420
\end{aligned}
$$
